guard: a log has no publish expectation until the principal's shared record is bound to it, and a handle that is no longer entitled to write its own log cannot move that shared record, and an abandonment that cannot reach the shared record refuses rather than clearing half of it
why: THE UNBOUND EXPECTATION IS THE DEFECT'S OWN SHAPE. A log is keyed per session; the subject it
publishes to is keyed per principal. Returning this log's own last ack when nothing is bound is
returning the exact number that took every agent's second session dark, and the argument for
allowing it was that no shipped path reaches it. That argument was true, and it is the same
argument the released seam shipped on: two correct components with an assumption standing where
a guard belongs. So the assumption is a guard.
THE ORDERING FINDING CAME OUT OF MAKING THAT GUARD REAL, WHICH IS WHY IT IS GRADED HERE. With
the fallback gone, a suite cell that had always passed went red and showed that the generation
guard ran inside `write`, AFTER the shared record moved. A handle whose file had been rewritten
underneath it advanced the PRINCIPAL's tip and only then learned it was not allowed to write.
The record belongs to every thread of that principal, so a refusal that arrives after the
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY. The suite imports `../src/event-wal.js` by relative source path, so the
bytes mutated are the bytes graded; no dist, no build in the command. Its only package import
for this behaviour is the in-memory double from @cotal-ai/smoke-kit, which is test-only and
carries none of the behaviour under test.

mutations.name: S16 an unbound log offers its own last ack instead of refusing
mutations.expectRed: [H] an UNBOUND log has no expectation and says so, rather than offering its own last ack
mutations.cell: [H] an UNBOUND log has no expectation and says so, rather than offering its own last ack
mutations.note: The released behaviour restored as a default. It is not reachable from any shipped path today, which is exactly why it needs a guard rather than a comment: the next caller is the one that reaches it. Its find carries the message's first line because `abandon` now refuses the unbound case in the same shape, so the two-line form no longer picks out one site.

mutations.cell: [H] ...and the PRINCIPAL's shared tip never moved for it
mutations.note: Removing the early check puts the generation guard back inside `write`, where it still refuses the write but only after the principal's shared tip has taken this handle's number. The sibling cell that asserts the refusal is a STALE-WRITER refusal is what makes this one legible: without it the mutant merely changes which error comes out.

mutations.note: Refusing it forces a caller that seeds a log and then starts an emitter over it to hold two handles on one file, which is exactly the state the generation guard refuses.

mutations.note: The cell uses a second record holding the SAME number on purpose: a check that compared tips rather than identity would pass here while accepting a genuinely different subject's record.
